theory.overview: A KD-Tree (K-dimensional tree) is a space-partitioning data structure for organizing points in k-dimensional space. It's a binary tree where each node is a k-dimensional point. Each level of the tree splits space along one dimension, cycling through dimensions. KD-Trees enable efficient nearest neighbor searches and range queries in low-dimensional spaces (typically k < 20). They're widely used in computer graphics, ray tracing, and spatial databases.

keyConcepts.name: Construction
keyConcepts.description: Find median along splitting dimension, make it root. Recursively build left/right subtrees from points before/after median. O(n log n) for balanced tree.

keyConcepts.name: Splitting Dimensions
keyConcepts.description: Cycle through dimensions at each level. For 2D: x, y, x, y, ... For 3D: x, y, z, x, y, z, ...

keyConcepts.name: Nearest Neighbor Search
keyConcepts.description: Traverse tree to find candidate. Check if hyperplane could contain closer point. Prune subtrees that cannot contain closer points. O(log n) average.

keyConcepts.name: Range Search
keyConcepts.description: Find all points within a query region. Recursively check subtrees that intersect the query region. O(n^(1-1/k) + m) where m is result size.

algorithmSteps.description: Root level (x-dim): Median x=13. Left: x < 13, Right: x > 13
Left subtree (y-dim): Median y=12. Split by y-coordinate
Recursively build until all points are leaves. Balanced tree of height 3.
Nearest neighbor to (7,14): Search tree, find (6,12) distance ≈ 2.24
Range query [5,15]×[10,20]: Return 3 points in region
